body.statement: Determine the largest \(\gamma^{\star}\) such that, for every \(\gamma<\gamma^{\star}\) and \(H_n\le n^\gamma\), the actual selected-PCR recursive construction satisfies \((\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}+(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)^2t_{\mathrm{rec},n}+d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), and construct a legal sequence in \(\mathcal C_n\) on which at least one term fails to vanish for every \(\gamma>\gamma^{\star}\).
body.justification: The sufficient exponent \(1/8\) is useful but may reflect conservative companion and Gram perturbation bounds; the sharp horizon-information boundary is genuinely unresolved.
body.gap: Shen (2026) holds the horizon fixed, and no adjacent PCR or Gaussian-comparison paper determines a maximal growing TWSF horizon for the implemented estimator.
body.consumer: A sharp exponent would determine how far a software ribbon may extrapolate as panel size grows and would separate estimator limitations from proof slack.

obligation.what_is_open: A legal sequence proving failure above the maximal exponent, and hence the exact value of the sharp exponent, is not derived.
obligation.obstruction: The recursive relative-Gram estimate is an upper perturbation bound. Its horizon-squared factor can result from the Jacobian Lipschitz bound and need not be attained by any member of the declared fixed-rank class. Therefore it cannot supply the lower failure sequence required by the open question.
obligation.attempted: The actual fitted three-piece temporal-Riesz decomposition and the persistent all-ones sequence were audited. They prove the stated upper rate, but the all-ones Jacobians align in one direction and do not yield a matching lower covariance error. No admissible fixed-rank alternative was found that both saturates the second-order companion perturbation and preserves the recovery, strong-spectrum, and power-boundedness conditions.
obligation.partial_result:
Fix \(\gamma<1/4\), let \(H_n\le n^\gamma\), and put \(b_n=\log(nH_n)\).  The proved recursive rates imply
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}=O(1),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(\frac{H_nb_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{H_n^2b_n}{n}\right),
\]
\[
 t_{\mathrm{rec},n}\vee\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(H_n^2\sqrt{\frac{b_n}{n}}\right).
\]
The Gaussian comparison lemma gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 =O_{\Pr}\!\left(
 \Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(2H_n/\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n})\}^{2/3}\right)=o_{\Pr}(1).
\]
Because \(2\gamma-1/2<0\), all displayed polynomial rates dominate their logarithmic factors.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\),
\[
 (\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 +(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)^2t_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 +d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=o_{\Pr}(1).
\]
Thus achievability holds for every exponent below \(1/4\); the unresolved part is a matching legal failure sequence above the sharp boundary.
